# Cross-release pattern recognition (qualitative) — R1 vs R2 vs R3

## Executive summary

The three war.gov UAP drops are best read not as a single growing pile of sightings but as three differently-packaged corpora with distinct centers of gravity. **R1** (158 records, 2026-05-08) is a sensor-and-form archive: military MISREPs and Range-Fouler debriefs from the CENTCOM/Persian Gulf theater (33% Middle East), 1947-50 "flying disc" check-lists, and legacy FBI Bureau files — granular, heavily redacted (66%), and self-documenting in prose. **R2** (64 records, 2026-05-22) is a near-mono-modal infrared video dump: ~80% DVIDS clips, 50% tagged "CENTCOM," 84% "redacted," with no object-descriptive bodies extracted on disk, so its apparent shape, geography, and redaction signals are largely packaging artifacts riding on identical congressional-request boilerplate. **R3** (72 records, 2026-06-12) abandons the Middle East entirely (0% CENTCOM), relocates the story to the continental US (56% CONUS), and introduces three things earlier drops lacked: an 18-record CIA Cold-War foreign-intelligence bloc, a genuine analytic/skeptical voice (AARO/ICA assessments that try to *explain* sightings), and AI-generated "digital renderings" of witness testimony. The connective tissue is real but thinner than it looks: R3 explicitly cites R1 as a source on the "Western US Event" and re-releases at least one CIA report (Sary Shagan, 1973) less-redacted — so the newest drop more often *deepens and re-frames* older material than it breaks genuinely new ground.

## Morphology and behaviour

Across the three drops the descriptive register collapses and then rebounds in a different form. R1 captures morphology in a rigid 1947-50 "Check-List — Unidentified Flying Objects" form with discrete fields — Shape, Color, Tactics, Maneuverability — yielding terse, columnar entries like dow-007's "Shapo Mushroom … Manner of disappoarance Disintegration" and dow-009's "Shapo disc-like or spherical … Color Silver." R2 carries almost no object-descriptive body text at all: all 51 video records have empty extracted bodies on disk, so their only morphology/kinematics signal is the uploader-defined title (dow-083 "4 UAP Formation Iran," dow-084 "Syrian UAP instant acceleration") plus a repeated ~600-character chain-of-custody boilerplate. R3 abandons the form for continuous prose: fbi-060 narrates "a red sphere … inside the red sphere, at the center … a 'white plasma sun' about the size of a basketball," and dow-137 writes "a luminous orange 'mother orb' appeared to produce smaller red 'orbs,' one after another."

There is a real directional shift toward self-luminous orbs in R3's narratives, but it is **not** a clean "dominant shape flip," and that overstatement should be dropped. The deterministic morphology counts in `release_patterns.md` actually put R3's disc (24%) and circular (25%) tags *at or above* sphere/orb (21%), and R1's leading tag is "circular" (36%), not disc (17%). R1's own "319.1 Flying Discs 1949" folder (dow-006) opens with spheres — "Two objects were sighted, both spherical in shape" — so the R1 baseline is a mixed metallic disc-and-sphere world, not a pure silver-saucer one. What *is* well-grounded is that R3's witness narratives skew toward emissive plasma orbs ("plasma-like sphere," fbi-063; "brilliant red sphere," fbi-064) where R1's vocabulary was reflective-metal ("silvery or aluminum," "reflected the sun's rays").

The "angular, non-symmetrical potato" is genuine and is R3's one named non-orb morphotype: ica-001 describes an object "resembling an angular, non-symmetrical potato made of uneven panels," and fbi-058 independently calls it "potato shaped … articulating fish scales or panels that were non-symmetrical, non-overlapping." But it should be characterized as translucent and shape-shifting ("slightly translucent, shimmering … while slowly changing shape," ica-001), not a "solid craft," and it is not the *only* structured-object description — the Western US orange orb (dow-141) "mechanically" expels smaller orbs.

The kinematic emphasis does move from single-object flight-tactics (R1: "Performed a tight circle … too tight a circle to be any type of known aircraft," dow-009) toward multi-object population dynamics in R3 — merging, launching, tandem formation (fbi-060: "saw the orbs merge together into one orb"). The "mother orb launching clusters of two-to-four red orbs" is real in dow-137, **but it is not introduced by R3 and is not a "self-replicating swarm with no R1 analogue"** — that claim is refuted. The identical phenomenon is already in R1's dow-082, whose "Orbs Launching Orbs" page records the orange "mother" orb launching red orbs in groups of two to four; dow-137 is explicitly a re-analysis of that same incident and cites R1's VIRIN as its reference. AARO's leading explanations are infrared countermeasure flares and Blue-Force/unrecognized tech, not biological replication, and the audit shows "split/multiply" behaviour at just 1/72 in R3.

> **Confidence & caveats.** R2's shape/behaviour vocabulary (spherical, formation, "tic tac," "instant acceleration") lives *only* in clip titles, not in any extracted body — so R2 should never be used as independent evidence of a morphology trend. Treat the morphology "rebound" in R3 as a register change (prose witness narratives) rather than a measured increase in any one shape class; the hard counts do not support a disc→orb flip.

## Geography and operational mode

The theater of operations flips decisively. R1 is anchored in the CENTCOM/Persian Gulf war zone (52 records, 33% Middle East) — wartime ISR like dow-044, a "Mission Report, Persian Gulf, August 2020" supporting NAVCENT against "IRIN/IRGCN vessels." R2 doubles down: 32 of 64 records (50%) carry the region tag "CENTCOM." R3 drops the theater **completely** — CENTCOM/Middle East falls to 0%, CONUS climbs to 56% — and this is one of the better-verified claims in the set: keyword scans of all 72 R3 records returned zero Iraq/Iran/Syria/Gulf incidents, and the six R3 files containing Middle-East strings are OCR noise or Gemini astronauts naming Earth landmarks from orbit, not Gulf UAP events.

Operationally this means R1's "operator-on-a-sensor" military model (aircrew, bullseye coordinates, ATFLIR lines, "no impact to mission") gives way in R3 to a law-enforcement/intelligence-community casework model. R3's CONUS incidents are owned by the FBI (40%) and CIA (25%) more than DoW (17%), documented on FD-302 and FD-1057 interview forms rather than cockpit MISREPs.

R3's homeland story is not one phenomenon but three operationally distinct clusters — a verdict-supported finding: (1) a military test-range "orbs launching orbs" event near "a sensitive national security site in the western United States" (dow-137, witnesses are federal law-enforcement agents); (2) a stationary daytime object over Cheyenne Mountain seen by "five U.S. Army service members at Fort Carson" (ica-001), i.e. NORAD-adjacent terrain; and (3) a multi-year residential Northeastern "plasma orb" flap with civilian backyard witnesses (fbi-060, fbi-066). These differ in witness type, setting, time of day, and AARO disposition.

> **Confidence & caveats.** R2's "50% Middle East" is partly a coarse-aggregation artifact: 32 clips are rolled under one "CENTCOM" macro-tag with near-identical congressional-request preambles. The adversarial check, however, **refutes the stronger claim that geography is "masked" or that there is "no per-clip narrative"**: 8 of the 32 clips name a specific country or body of water in their titles (Iran, Syria, Afghanistan, Kabul, Persian Gulf), and 31 of 32 carry a unique timestamped "Video Description" in the full manifest that the truncated 600-char catalog summaries hide. So describe R2's Middle-East concentration as a real-but-coarsely-bucketed theater signal, not a fabricated one.

## Agency and evidentiary mode

Each drop is dominated by a different evidentiary posture. R1 is overwhelmingly raw collection — 80 DoW MISREPs (51%), FD-302 interviews, FBI Bureau files — with little adjudication. R2 has even less analysis: a 51-clip DVIDS video dump whose lone CIA IIR (cia-001) explicitly disclaims evaluation ("THIS IS AN INFORMATION REPORT, NOT FINALLY EVALUATED INTELLIGENCE"). R3 debuts a genuine analytic layer.

The headline R3 novelty is the ICA agency and its AARO IC-partner assessment (ica-001) that actively tries to *explain away* a UAP, attributing the Colorado Springs object to "sunlight backscattering, where sunlight reflecting from mountain snow cover illuminated the underside of low-altitude clouds," held "with low confidence." This is the only document in the entire extracted corpus using the formal estimative phrase "low confidence," so as the first fully-reasoned, multi-page, formally-graded prosaic explanation it is genuinely new to R3. **But the claim that R3 is the *first release to explain away a UAP at all* should be softened** — it is refuted as written. R1 already contains prosaic government attributions: dow-070 is titled "Resolved as an Aircraft, Middle East 2013," and dow-077's "AARO Comment" attributes an apparent size increase to "the U.S. platform closing the distance." The accurate framing: R3 is the first to offer an *affirmative, formally-graded* explain-away of an entire object, not the first prosaic explanation in the archive.

The CIA contribution is the clearest structural shift, and it verifies cleanly: **0 records in R1, 1 incidental IIR in R2, 18 records (25%) in R3** — "a quarter" of the newest drop. The R3 CIA bloc is a Cold-War HUMINT/policy archive, not new sightings: foreign field reports (cia-007 Baku triangular craft, cia-012 Sary Shagan), policy monographs (cia-003 Robertson "Scientific Advisory Panel"; cia-004 "U-2 and OXCART Programs, 1954-1974," which reframes UFOs as misidentified spyplanes). One precision correction: not all 18 fall in 1950-1974 — 15 do, while cia-002 is a July 2008 Harare cable, cia-013 a November 1976 IIR, and cia-016 (Blue Book Special Report No. 14) is undated. Report it as "18 CIA files, mostly Cold-War (15 dated c. 1950-74), plus a 1976 IIR and a 2008 cable."

The FBI rotates form across drops: largely archival Bureau case files plus one modern FD-302 in R1, entirely absent in R2 (0 records), then a full modern investigative suite in R3 — FD-302 interviews *and* FD-1057 records in which agents log their *own* first-hand observation (fbi-069: "SA — and SA — observed what they believed to be a UAP … a bright white light above a bright red light"). The "congressional/legal" bucket is a trap: R2's 80% share is the video boilerplate, whereas R3's single USG record (usg-001) is the archive's first authentic White House/Senate correspondence file — and its content is institutional *denial* ("there was no evidence indicating that sightings categorized as 'unidentified' were extraterrestrial vehicles").

R3 also uniquely routes one event through a multi-agency stack: Colorado Springs appears as an FBI FD-302 ("bean shaped," fbi-065), an FD-1057 plus digital-rendering pipeline (fbi-058/059), and the ICA/AARO backscatter analysis (ica-001), with the note "AARO has since been in contact with the interviewee."

## Cross-release narrative threads

The connective tissue is real but should be stated precisely. The strongest documented bridge is the **Western US "orbs launching orbs" event**: R1 plants a data-thin slide deck (dow-082, which itself admits "there is no technical data directly associated with this report"); R3 returns with a formal AARO Unresolved Case Analysis (dow-137), five raw witness statements (dow-139–143), and ~12 FBI renderings. dow-137 explicitly footnotes R1 — "References: (a) https://www.war.gov/ufo/#Western-US-Event … VIRIN: 260508-D-D0360-1052, 08-MAY 2026" — the date stamp matching R1's release. The "up to 40 percent unrecognized technology" figure is real but should be reported as *hedged*: the memo labels it "(Pending)," a "preliminary exclusion-based hypothesis … unsubstantiated by technical data," with the case "unresolved." Use "may explain up to 40%," not "concludes."

A subtlety the lenses surface: the catalog treats "Western US orbs" as one mega-thread, but it is two unrelated incidents — an **Oct-2023 ground-agent sighting** (no sensor data; matured R1→R3) and a **Late-2025 helicopter/IR event** (matured R1→R2). The Late-2025 event's hardest evidence (FD-302 fbi-053; 24 IR stills fbi-029–052) lands in R1; R2's odni-001 is the *same official's* prose retelling that openly back-references the R1 imagery ("originally released on war.gov/UFO on May 8, 2026"). So this thread runs backwards from the usual pattern — corroboration by restatement, with no independent sensor confirmation.

Two R3 threads have no antecedent at all. **Colorado Springs** arrives as a complete self-contained R3 package — vivid testimony *and* the skeptical backscatter verdict in the same drop, pre-empting cross-release momentum. The "nearly identical panelled-potato" language across fbi-058 and ica-001 is verified, with one caveat: both trace to the *same* five-person Army witness group, so "independent IC analyst" means a different agency channel, not an independent observation. The **Northeastern orbs** thread is genuinely R3-original (FD-302s plus civilian video clips, cross-referenced as "the same general area"), though the video bodies are empty so the evidentiary weight rests on the paired narratives.

Conversely the **Persian Gulf 2020 thread** peaks in R1 (structured MISREPs) and is then abandoned: R2's apparent "expansion" is ~30 raw FLIR clips sharing one note that the materials "lack a substantiated chain-of-custody," and R3 drops the Gulf entirely.

Named entities reinforce the bridges: AARO moves from invisible provenance stamp to named signatory; the **Sary Shagan CIA report** appears twice (R2 cia-001 redacted, R3 cia-012 named and de-redacted, same serial FIRK-311/01638); the **1948-50 New Mexico "green fireball"/Project Twinkle** case refracts through FBI file 62-HQ-83894 (R1), OSI/Sandia correspondence to "Lt. Colonel Doyle Rees" (R2), and USAF incident summaries (R3); and R3 names J. Edgar Hoover, McDivitt, and the Sary Shagan range outright where R1 used "the Director" and an unnamed "range."

## Historical reach

The intuitive reading — "R3 reaches deeper into the past" — is half-wrong and should be stated carefully. All three drops span roughly 1945-2026, and **R1 actually holds the single earliest incident**: dow-003, a WWII foo-fighter file ("night phenomena (foofighters) … 415th Night Fighter Squadron," 3/18/45). R3's earliest is 1949. What changes in R3 is *density*, not the floor: 1950s rise from 3% to 18% and 1960s from 6% to 15%, and this mid-century mass is overwhelmingly **CIA-driven** — the same 0→1→18 agency shift described above. R2's apparent reach to 1961-63 (Mercury audio) is a packaging artifact: those items are raw audio clips with no extracted text (nasa-022 is just a recovery team "discussing a dye pack"), so only R3 actually delivers *readable* early-1960s astronaut debriefings (Gemini 4: "sparkles everywhere … it looked like an artificial starlit sky," which the crew self-attribute to fuel/urine particles).

R3 also fills the late-20th/early-21st-century window from a new angle — a 1998 White House/Congressional correspondence file (usg-001) and the archive's most recent CIA incident, a July 2008 Harare airport case (cia-002) — even as it is simultaneously the most mid-century-heavy drop.

## Disclosure posture

R3's redaction rate collapses (R1 66% → R2 84% → R3 17%), but this is a **composition artifact, not a policy change**. The redaction-notice text is byte-identical across all three releases and maps 1:1 to the redaction flag. R3 looks open because its mass (CIA Cold-War files, NASA debriefs, 1949 saucer studies) was already cleared — cia-016 states its content "has been available on CIA's public website," and several files bear "Approved for Release 2026 Under Section 1842 of the NDAA FY2024." Every one of R3's 12 still-redacted files is contemporary domestic FBI/AARO/ICA/USG casework; CIA (0/18) and NASA (0/11) carry zero war.gov redaction. Where R3 *does* redact, it removes only PII and facility identity while preserving the phenomenon description in full — fbi-058 blacks out the witness but keeps "articulating fish scales or panels" that "cloaked."

Two further posture shifts are R3-specific. The "Featured" flag (10 hero records) is an editorial spine, not an openness signal — 4 of the 10 are themselves redacted (fbi-058, fbi-060, fbi-061, ica-001) — so Featured tracks narrative importance, not transparency. And R3 publishes its own skeptical/"debunking" doctrine as meta-evidence: cia-003's Robertson-panel recommendation "to strip the Unidentified Flying Objects of the special status they have been given," its modern descendant in the ICA backscatter assessment, and the 1998 USG denials. The transparency is paired with deliberate hedging: the marquee analysis is explicitly "low confidence" and the flagship case "remains unresolved as of June 2026."

> **Confidence & caveats.** R2's 84% redaction headline is largely meaningless: 58 of 64 records are videos with no body to redact, so the flag rides on boilerplate. Do not read R2 as the "most censored" drop — it is the least *self-documenting* one.

## Sensor and collection modality

The dominant capture modality flips across drops, and this is one of the more analytically important threads. R1 is the most sensor-diverse (photographic 47%, radar 30%, IR/FLIR 20%), built on primary instrument captures — fbi-021 is "a still image derived from a U.S. government system" with a "central crosshair reticle." R2 collapses to a near-mono-modal FLIR feed (IR/FLIR 77%, video 77%). R3 swings to a paper-and-picture mix (photographic 33%, satellite/space 21%, radar 19%) with video/sensor feed at **0%**, and introduces a categorically new modality: AI "digital renderings" (fbi-073–082) and "digital recreations" (fbi-085/086).

The provenance implication is significant. R1/R2 imagery is captured *from the phenomenon* (sensor-to-file). R3's signature imagery is generated *from human memory*: fbi-059 is "an artistic interpretation … derived from the first-hand narrative description" in fbi-058, and the DoW Notional Map states outright, "All images were artificially generated using https//genai.mil/ … Phenomena are enlarged for illustrative purposes and are not to relative scale … All locations are notional" (dow-138). The government itself flags R3's hero visuals as illustrative, not evidentiary — a verifiability disclaimer absent from R1's measurable sensor geometry ("slant range of 4.06NM … IR sensor was set to black hot," dow-031). Tellingly, R3 admits primary witness video *exists* (fbi-060 cites attached footage PR004) yet releases an AI recreation in its place. The readable substance of R3 is therefore the witness statements, not the pictures.

## What Release 03 changes about the overall picture

- **It moves the story home and changes who is telling it.** The corpus pivots from a foreign battlespace narrated by aircrew on sensors (R1/R2) to a CONUS narrative owned by FBI and CIA casework — interviews, site surveys, and AARO memos replace cockpit MISREPs. The Middle-East corpus is not expanded; it is dropped.

- **It adds an analytic/skeptical voice the archive previously lacked** — but a hedged one. R3 is the first drop with formally-graded resolution attempts (ica-001's "low confidence" backscatter explain-away) and the government's own "debunking" doctrine (cia-003). Crucially, the flagship cases remain officially *unresolved*, so increased adjudication does not mean increased certainty.

- **It deepens more than it discovers.** The marquee thread (Western US orbs) is explicitly a re-analysis of an R1 hero case, and at least one CIA report is the same 1973 document re-released less-redacted. Much of R3's apparent novelty is older material surfaced more openly, not net-new phenomena.

- **It shifts the evidentiary center of gravity from sensor to witness.** Video/sensor feed drops to 0% while R3 introduces openly AI-generated renderings of human testimony — and substitutes a recreation even where real witness video is admitted to exist. The newest "evidence" is one step further from the phenomenon, not closer.

- **Its transparency is compositional, not policy-driven.** The redaction collapse to 17% reflects a corpus that was already declassified (CIA/NASA), while every genuinely sensitive new domestic file stays redacted at R1-era rates. R3 is differently *packaged*, not categorically more candid about UAP.
